dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: tantryādivādyaśabdeṣu dīrgheṣu kramasaṃsthiteḥ | ananyacetāḥ pratyante paravyomavapur bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: One who listens with undivided mind to the long, sustained sounds of stringed and other instruments, following them through their unfolding, becomes at their very end a body of supreme space.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh's notes: a well-produced note seems to come out of eternity and to disappear into it, and when the music stops it still vibrates in memory; if the mind stays with that echo instead of wandering, one is absorbed in the source of all sound (parāvāk). Wallis glosses tantrī as a stringed instrument such as a vīṇā or tambura.
dharana.technique_name: Following a Long Musical Note to Its End
dharana.instruction: Listen to one long note until it disappears, and stay in the space it leaves.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 41 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the onset of a sustained note
the edge where it becomes inaudible
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the life of one long note: onset, resonance, fading edge, and the space after it. Attention travels with the note and stays at its end.
geometry.svg_hint: a long tapering line that thins to nothing, with an open field after its tip
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Ride the resonance out
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: attention rides one sound all the way out and is left in open space when the sound ends. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever it is when the note becomes inaudible
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn toward one sustained sound and stay with it
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.gaze: Eyes closed, or resting on the instrument
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: One long note: a plucked string, a singing bowl, or a recorded drone, followed to its last trace
attention.secondary: The space that is left when the sound has gone

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: One who listens with undivided mind to the long, sustained sounds of stringed and other instruments, following them through their unfolding, becomes at their very end a body of supreme space.
adiyogi.method_summary: Sound or play one long, sustained note (a string, a bowl, a recorded drone). Listen to it with undivided attention as it unfolds and thins. When it becomes inaudible, do not move on; stay in what remains. Repeat with the next note.

honesty.disclosure: Door 018 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 18 (verse 41) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 018 is dharana 18, verse 41. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Keep the volume comfortable; do not hold the ear close to a loud instrument. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 018: following a long musical note to its end. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 18, verse 41.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Any easy seat. The map is one note: its start, its long resonance, its fading edge, and the space after.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor or the chair carry you. Eyes closed or soft.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Strike or play one long note. Go with it all the way. When you can no longer hear it, stay right there.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: attention rides a sound out into open space. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 41: listen with undivided mind to the long sounds of strings and other instruments; at their end one becomes a body of supreme space.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Let the breath go unwatched for a round. Move the fingers and toes. Return to the room.
